title: Sell Mineral Rights in Evans, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Evans, CO | Weld County Wattenberg
metaDescription: Own minerals near Evans, just south of Greeley in the Wattenberg field? We price your interest off decline data from your actual royalty checks.
heroLead: Evans sits just south of Greeley inside the Wattenberg field's productive core, dense enough with horizontal units that most mineral owners here already have some production history to price against.
intro: If you own minerals near Evans, the value question usually comes down to two numbers: your net revenue interest and how far along the decline curve the well or unit is sitting. Both come straight from your division order and check stubs, which is why we ask for them before quoting anything meaningful.

This part of Weld County has seen dense multi-well pad development for over a decade, so it is common for a single tract to sit inside more than one unit over time as operators re-drill or add wells to existing pads.

sections.heading: Reading your decline curve
paragraphs: A Wattenberg horizontal well typically produces most of its lifetime volume in the first two to three years, then settles into a long, flatter tail. Where your well sits on that curve matters more than the county it is in. A three-year-old well and a twelve-year-old well with the same current net revenue interest will not price the same.

sections.heading: Multiple wells, one tract
paragraphs: If your acreage has been added to more than one unit over the years, your division order should reflect a separate interest for each. We check every unit your tract touches so the offer captures full value rather than pricing off just the most recent one.

sections.heading: Comparable sale activity
paragraphs: Beyond decline-curve math, we also weigh recent comparable Weld County mineral sales to make sure our offer is grounded against what similar interests are actually trading for right now, not a static formula.

sections.heading: Selling part of your interest
paragraphs: Some Evans-area owners prefer to sell only a portion of a mineral interest rather than the whole thing, keeping a stake in future production while still getting cash today. We can structure an offer either way, a full buyout or a partial interest sale, depending on what fits your situation.

faqs.question: What documents speed up my offer the most?
faqs.answer: A recent division order and a few months of check stubs. Together they show your exact interest and current production trend.

faqs.question: My well is older. Is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the price reflects remaining production on the decline tail rather than early-life volumes.

faqs.question: What if I'm in more than one unit?
faqs.answer: We evaluate each unit separately and roll them into a single combined offer for your total interest.

faqs.question: How current is your pricing?
faqs.answer: We weigh recent comparable Weld County sales alongside decline-curve math so the offer reflects current market activity.

faqs.question: Can I sell just part of my interest instead of all of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly structure partial sales so owners keep a share of future production while still getting cash for the rest.
